title: Phase 6-7 Challenge, native bridge and shipping
area: Weather dares (dare_generator), all native work across the redesign, and shipping (builds, store, review, testing)

keyFacts.fact: Dares today live entirely in web/ui/ranks.js. DARE_LIFE has 5 life dares, including a 'cold' shower finish. dareMuscle picks a muscle that is trained, untouched 21+ days and not recovering. dareToday makes one seeded pick per day: a lift dare half the time if a muscle qualifies, otherwise a life dare. dareText writes Coach/Drill copy, and uiDareHTML/uiWireDare give Accept / Not today, then Done / Start now. There is no weather, location, objective list or reward.
keyFacts.ref: web/ui/ranks.js:226-300 (DARE_LIFE 233-239, dareMuscle 241-246, dareToday 247-264, dareText 265-275, uiDareHTML 276-289, uiWireDare 290-300)

keyFacts.fact: The dare is a card on the Body/Home page, between Today and the check-in. The onboarding voice step sets its tone.

Shape of S.dares: {scale:0.5..1, tone:'coach'|'drill', won:number, cur:{d:'YYYY-MM-DD', kind:'lift'|'life', st:'new'|'yes'|'no'|'done', lift → k,ex,sets,reps,kg,days; life → id,sc}}. 'Not today' multiplies scale by 0.85. Done adds 0.05 to scale and 1 to won.

Andrej's dare rules: once a day; half are lift dares (at most 1.5x logged reps and 80% of best weight), otherwise a life dare; Coach by default, Drill on a switch; it roasts the neglect, never the person; 'Not today' costs nothing and shrinks the next dare.
There is no XP or other currency. A done dare is only marked done. Rank points (RP) exist per muscle only. '+50 GRIT' would be a new currency.
expo-location is not installed, there is no location plugin in app.json, and ios.infoPlist has only camera and Health strings (no NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription).

keyFacts.fact: react-native-webview 13.16.1 has no iOS geolocation support. geolocationEnabled exists only in AndroidWebViewProps, and the iOS native code never mentions geolocation. In-page geolocation would therefore use plain WKWebView: it needs the Info.plist key (a build) and WebKit adds its own per-site prompt naming 'ossa.app'.
keyFacts.ref: node_modules/react-native-webview/src/WebViewTypes.ts:947 (AndroidWebViewProps), :1003 (geolocationEnabled); grep of node_modules/react-native-webview/apple finds no geolocation

keyFacts.fact: The WebView loads {html, baseUrl:'https://ossa.app/'} with originWhitelist ['*']. The built page has no Content-Security-Policy, and it already fetches external HTTPS (Mixpanel). I checked with curl on 16 Oct: api.open-meteo.com, geocoding-api.open-meteo.com and api.met.no all return Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, so the page can call them directly. App Transport Security is satisfied because all three are HTTPS.

LICENSING CONFLICT with ground rule 4: Open-Meteo's free API is for non-commercial use only, and apps with subscriptions count as commercial. Ossa sells Ossa Pro. Commercial use needs a paid plan through customer-api.open-meteo.com with an &apikey= parameter. The pricing page gives no prices. The free tier allows 10,000 calls a day.

MET Norway's data is CC BY 4.0, which allows commercial use with credit. Mobile apps must identify themselves in the User-Agent, keep coordinates to 4 decimals at most, cache until the Expires time, and move to a caching proxy once traffic grows. The WebView supports applicationNameForUserAgent, and a native fetch in App.js can set the User-Agent directly.

Web → native messages handled in App.js: buzz{p}, hello, remind{on,list,ask}, widget{snap}, widget:pin, health:connect, health:read, health:settings (the web never sends this one), iap:offerings, iap:buy{pkg}, iap:restore, iap:manage, link{url} (https: or mailto: only), pose:get{f,i}, share:image{b64,name}. Injected before page load: navigator.vibrate rerouted to buzz, a navigator.userActivation stub, and window.OSSA_NATIVE={platform}.

Native → web messages (injectJavaScript calling window.OssaNative.recv, queued until 'hello'): caps{platform,expoGo,notif,widget,health,healthSrc,iap}, pro{...}, health{...}, remind{granted,count,asked}, widget:pin{ok}, iap:offerings, iap:result, iap:restore, pose:chunk, fg (app back in front), open{go}. The web side handles them in nrecv.

Exports in native/*.js. reminders: permission, schedule, clear, onOpen. health.ios: source, status, connect, read, openSettings; it reads only StepCount, SleepAnalysis and RestingHeartRate. purchases: available, ENTITLEMENT='pro', setup, summarise, status, offerings, buy, restore, manage. pose: chunk, shareImage. widget.ios: NAME, available, register, update, pin. widget-shared: KEY, C, dayKey, saveSnap, loadSnap, todayOf, fresh, lines, dotColour. OssaWidget.ios: default createWidget('OssaBody').

keyFacts.fact: Notification taps and deep links already work, including from a cold start. Reminders.onOpen reads getLastNotificationResponse plus a listener. ossa://<word> URLs match /^ossa:\/\/([a-z]+)/. Both send {t:'open',go} to nativeOpen, which knows review, train, score, check, desk, scan and pro, and falls back to Today (ignored during onboarding). The scheme 'ossa' is set in app.json.

Local notifications are planned entirely in the web page. remindPlan() = remindPlan0() + deskPlan(), up to 60 items of {at,title,body,go}. Native cancels everything and reschedules on each sync with DATE triggers, skipping items less than 30 s away. Every save() calls nativeSoon, which resends the list after 1.6 s if it changed. So a one-off nudge 45 minutes after a workout is a web-only change.

Haptics mapping: an array becomes one Success notification haptic. A single number ≤6 is a selection tap, ≤10 a light impact, anything larger a medium impact. Pulse.beat() already buzzes 10 per heartbeat. expo-haptics offers Soft, Rigid and Heavy, but App.js never uses them, and there is no custom-pattern API.

A native share sheet already exists. The web sends share:image with a base64 PNG, which is written to the cache and opened with React Native's Share.share({url}). The posture card uses it. Body.snapshot() and Body.glowShot() return a PNG of our 3D body, so the trading card needs no build.
Apple Health resting heart rate (7-day average) is already read and stored in S.health.rhr and S.bpm. That is enough for the heartbeat screen without new HealthKit types.

app.json: name 'Ossa', version '1.0.0', no ios.buildNumber, root backgroundColor '#000000', userInterfaceStyle dark. There is no 'splash' key and no expo-splash-screen plugin; by the SDK 57 docs the default splash background is white #ffffff (unconfirmed on the phone). App.js already paints its root and the WebView #000, and expo-system-ui is installed.

eas.json: appVersionSource 'remote'. Profiles: development (dev client, internal), preview (internal), production (autoIncrement). submit.production has ascAppId 6818619462. expo-updates is not installed, so every change, web-only ones included, reaches TestFlight only through a new EAS build. Expo Go runs the latest App.js and web code from the PC, but not widgets, HealthKit or RevenueCat.

build-for-app-store.bat runs build-html and then 'eas build --platform ios --profile production --auto-submit'. That uploads to TestFlight only and is not a review submission; Andrej runs it himself and types his own credentials.

Store files: store/APP-STORE-LISTING.md holds the name, subtitle, promo text, description, keywords, screenshot order, the six-section review notes, the privacy label and a pre-submit checklist. Screenshot folders: 6.3in-v2 (6 shots, 1206x2622), 6.9in-v2 (6, 1320x2868), the old 6.9in set (5) and google-play. No script in scripts/ makes screenshots and no doc says how they were made (unconfirmed). Settings has a 'Load demo data' button that would suit store shots.

keyFacts.fact: For review: the notes' screen recording shows the old app, the header image is old art, and the 8 Oct rejection reason isn't written down anywhere. Review note §6 names the fonts Archivo/Geist. The licences screen credits only MediaPipe.

There are no automated tests: no *.test/*.spec files and no test script. The only check is lint:tokens (scripts/check-tokens.js). .claude/launch.json defines 'ossa-preview' (node scripts/preview-server.js, port 5178), which rebuilds the page on every request. In the browser preview NATIVE.on is false, so every native call does nothing.
Git holds only one 'Initial commit' (b9b62ea). Almost every project file is modified or untracked, so there is no history to roll the redesign back to.

The native widgets hard-code the old palette (mint #9BFCEC, amber, background #05090B) and the old Body Score layout. Widgets were deliberately left for a native build. The streak screen already advertises a rank-body widget that doesn't exist yet. The widget's body picture is a PNG the web draws (figSvg), so its colours can change without a build.

items.name: dare_generator (weather dares)
items.today: Home shows one dare card (web/ui/shell.js:210) built by uiDareHTML (web/ui/ranks.js:276-289): a single line of text, Accept / Not today, then Done (or Start now for lift and mobility dares), with a Coach/Drill switch. The daily pick is seeded in dareToday (ranks.js:247-264). Life dares include a cold-shower finish (ranks.js:234). There is no weather, location, objective list or reward; a done dare only increments S.dares.won (ranks.js:295). No full-screen dare page exists.

changes.change: Move the dare block (ranks.js:225-300) here unchanged so dares have one owner, then extend it. Add WX_DARES: {id:'rain'|'cold'|'wind'|'sun'|'heat'|'indoor', name ('Storm Resistance', 'Cold Front', 'Headwind', 'Daylight', 'Heat Check', 'Indoor Day'), test(w), obj(scale)→[objective…], coach, drill}. Add a safety gate wxSafe(w) that allows no outdoor dare in thunder, heavy or freezing rain, sleet, heavy snow, fog, gusts ≥50 km/h, temperatures below 0 °C or above 30 °C, or after dark; those days get 'indoor' or the normal life dare.

Redefine dareToday(): lift dares keep Andrej's rules exactly. On the life half, if S.dares.wxOn and the S.wx reading is fresh, notable and safe, pick a kind:'wx' dare scaled by S.dares.scale; otherwise use today's DARE_LIFE. Still one dare a day, and 'Not today' still costs nothing.

Redefine dareText() and uiDareHTML() for kind 'wx'. The Home card shows a weather pill and the title; tapping it opens the full-screen dare. uiWireDare gains objective ticks; when every objective is ticked, st becomes 'done' (same scale and won rules as today) and S.dares.wxWon[id] goes up by 1.

New full-screen page openDare(), built as '#dareP' with class 'panel u-own' (the rkPanel pattern in ranks.js:46-52) so the closePanels wrapper (ranks.js:100) closes it. Contents: back button; pill with town and temperature ('LONDON, UK · 8 °C'); a 'Weather dare' eyebrow in the cyan token; the headline; a line with the real conditions; an objectives card with checkboxes and the reward label (per the open question); a safety line; Accept Dare / Not today; and the weather-data credit.

Objectives tick themselves where the app has data: steps through hSteps(0) counted from the moment of acceptance (Apple Health), water through the water log (waterToday, shell.js:192), mobility through a finished flow (mobilitySession, ossa.html:7567). Other objectives are ticked by hand.

wxGet(): get the place (loc:get through the bridge, or a typed town), then the weather (wx:get through the bridge, or a direct fetch with a 6 s AbortController timeout). Cache in S.wx for 60 minutes; if offline, use a reading up to 6 hours old and say when it was taken ('8 °C at 08:10'); after that, no weather dare. Only fetch while Home or the dare page is on screen (MET's rule against fetching when the app isn't in use).

Wrap phoneCard() and wirePhone() (ossa.html:10369, 10383) to add a 'Weather dares' row: Off / Use my location / Type your town. Wrap ossNotices() (ossa.html:7350) to add the weather-data credit (CC BY 4.0) and Inter's OFL notice.

Styles for the dare page from tokens.css only: glass card, checkbox, pill, big italic headline. The weather glyph is an SVG (rain, cold, wind, sun) with CSS rain streaks, static when reduced motion is on. Must pass check-tokens.
Include markers only: '/*@include ui/dares.css*/' after line 3350 and '/*@include ui/dares.js*/' after line 11875 (after ranks.js), so the later declarations win.
Delete lines 225-300 once they live in dares.js (or keep them and let dares.js override). Nothing else changes.
Add weather rules, safety thresholds and the S.dares/S.wx shapes to the Dares section; log the weather source, currency and opt-in decisions.

items.nativeBuildWhy: The screen, the weather logic and the typed-town path are web-only and work in the desktop preview and Expo Go. 'Use my location' and native weather fetching come from the Location item, which goes into the native build.
dependsOn: Currency decision (GRIT vs a shared XP from the Focus phase)
Trophy room (Evolve phase) for a 'Weatherproof' trophy, optional
stateChanges: S.dares.wxOn: boolean. Starts false and turns true once the user allows location or types a town (opt-in).

S.dares.cur for a weather dare: {d:'YYYY-MM-DD', kind:'wx', id:'rain'|'cold'|'wind'|'sun'|'heat'|'indoor', st:'new'|'yes'|'no'|'done', sc:number, acc:ms|null (when accepted), wx:{place:'London, UK', t:8, code:string|number, gust:number, day:boolean, at:ms}, obj:[{id:'walk'|'breathe'|'steps'|'water'|'flow', t:'10-minute walk outside', s:'Dress for the weather.', done:false, auto:'steps'|'water'|'flow'|null, base:number|null}]}. kind 'lift' and 'life' are unchanged, so old saves still work.
S.dares.wxWon: {rain:n, cold:n, wind:n, sun:n, heat:n}, for trophies.

S.wx: {place:{name:'London', region:'GB', lat:51.51, lon:-0.13, src:'gps'|'typed'}, at:ms, exp:ms, src:'met'|'open-meteo', cur:{t:8.2, code:'lightrain'|61, gust:24, precip:0.4, day:true}}. Coordinates are rounded to 2 decimal places (about 1 km).
Reward: if Andrej picks one shared XP, S.xp={total:n, log:[{d, src:'dare'|'monk'|…, n}]}, owned by the Focus phase. Otherwise there is no new field.
risks: The weather source licence (see the open question). Open-Meteo's free tier can't legally ship in an app with a subscription.
A wrong mapping from weather code to dare could send someone out in a storm. Hence one tested gate and a node check of all severe codes (see Testing).
Weather changes during the day while the dare is fixed at first open: show the time of the reading.
Auto-ticking steps needs Apple Health; without it, the objective is ticked by hand.
Rendering the Home card must not block on the network: draw with the cached reading, then update.
Cold-exposure wording in review (guideline 1.4.1). Keep it non-medical, opt-in and never in severe weather.
The privacy label and privacy policy may need 'Coarse Location' if coordinates leave the phone.
designDeviations: Background storm photo hotlinked from media.screensdesign.com: use a token-coloured SVG weather glyph and light CSS rain on black instead (ground rule 1, no stock renders).

'Environment conditions: Severe' and 'Locate Storm Center': dares never run in severe weather, so the line shows the real reading ('Light rain · 8 °C') and that objective is dropped. It is unsafe and the app can't check it; its slot goes to something the app can check, such as 'Add 1,500 steps' (Apple Health) or 'Two glasses of water when you're back' (water log).
'Verification complete': dropped, because the app has nothing to verify.
'No heavy outer layers. Let the skin sense the storm.': becomes 'Dress for the weather. Keep a brisk pace.' No advice to underdress.
'Stoic Stance · 1-min deep breathing in rain': becomes 'One minute of slow breathing outside. Under cover is fine.'
'Level up your grit by exposing your character to the elements': becomes 'Ten minutes out in it, then back in the warm.' (short, plain, no claims).
'WEATHER-TRIGGERED EVENT': becomes 'Weather dare'.
'+50 GRIT': waits on the currency decision. Until then, show 'Counts towards Weatherproof (2 of 5)' or nothing.

Add 'Not today' next to 'Accept Dare' (Andrej's rule: saying no costs nothing), a safety line ('Skip it if you feel unwell or it's icy underfoot. Head in if you start shivering.') and a weather-data credit.
'London, UK • 8°C' stays, using the user's own place and the live reading, written '8 °C'.
items.showAtEnd: Four 390x844 preview screenshots, each next to design/redesign-v2/images/dare_generator.png: (1) a rain dare, (2) the 'too wild out, here's an indoor dare' fallback, (3) the no-location state (type your town), (4) the Home card. Plus a 20-second iPhone recording in Expo Go: allow approximate location, the pill fills in, Accept, tick the objectives, Done. Plus the output of the severe-weather check (every severe case gives an indoor dare).

items.name: Location and weather source (system)
items.today: None. No expo-location, no NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription, and no iOS geolocation support in react-native-webview (WebViewTypes.ts:947, :1003). The page can fetch external HTTPS (ossa.html:10246). I checked CORS for Open-Meteo and MET Norway on 16 Oct.

changes.change: Add expo-location with 'npx expo install expo-location', after Andrej says go. It is first-party and included in Expo Go.

Add plugin ['expo-location', {locationWhenInUsePermission: 'Ossa uses your approximate location to check the weather for your daily dare. It's rounded to your area and only used for the forecast.'}], and ios.infoPlist 'NSLocationDefaultAccuracyReduced': true so iOS hands Ossa approximate location only. If Android ever ships, block ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION.

status() returns 'ok', 'denied', 'undetermined' or 'needs-build'. get(ask): requestForegroundPermissionsAsync only when ask is true; then getLastKnownPositionAsync({maxAge: 3 h, requiredAccuracy: 5000}), falling back to getCurrentPositionAsync({accuracy: Accuracy.Lowest}); round to 2 decimal places; reverseGeocodeAsync gives the label {name: city or subregion, region: isoCountryCode}. find(q): geocodeAsync(q) for a typed town, up to 5 results with labels (Apple's geocoder, no key).

changes.file: native/weather.js (new; only if MET Norway through native fetch)
changes.change: Fetch https://api.met.no/weatherapi/locationforecast/2.0/compact with the header User-Agent 'Ossa/<version> https://getossa.app'. Keep Expires and Last-Modified (If-Modified-Since) in AsyncStorage. Return a summary {ok, t, code (symbol_code), gust, precip, day, at}.

Import ./native/location (and ./native/weather). Add loc: await Loc.status() to caps (lines 52-61). New handlers in onMessage: 'loc:get' {ask} replies {t:'loc', ok, lat, lon, place, acc}; 'loc:find' {q} replies {t:'loc:find', q, list}; 'wx:get' {lat, lon} replies {t:'wx', ...}. Each must also reply with {ok:false, why} in the catch at lines 122-126. If the web page calls MET directly instead, add applicationNameForUserAgent='Ossa' to the WebView (line 160).

Wrap nrecv (ossa.html:10093) to take loc, loc:find and wx before the original handler; window.OssaNative.recv looks nrecv up by name at call time (ossa.html:10080), so the wrapper works. Add a promise helper like iapAsk (ossa.html:10136) with a timeout. In the browser preview (NATIVE.on false), use navigator.geolocation (localhost counts as secure) or Open-Meteo geocoding and forecast, for development only.

items.nativeBuildWhy: A new native module (expo-location) and new Info.plist strings. Any App.js change also ships only in a binary, since there is no expo-updates. It can be tried in Expo Go first, where expo-location is included but the prompt shows Expo Go's own wording.
newFiles: native/weather.js (if MET Norway through native fetch)
stateChanges: S.wx.place (see dare_generator), stored rounded; raw coordinates are never stored
risks: App Store guideline 5.1.1: the purpose string must say exactly why. Location is optional, and the typed town is the fallback when it's denied.
Approximate location can be several km off. Fine for weather, but the place label can name a nearby town.
Reverse and forward geocoding need the network and Apple rate-limits them. Cache the label in S.wx.place.
geocodeAsync without permission on iOS: the docs only state a permission requirement for Android (unconfirmed for iOS).
MET traffic rules (≤20 requests/s across all installs; a proxy once traffic is large). Hourly caching and fetching only while in use keep the launch well under that.

If the coordinates go to a weather service, the App Privacy label probably needs 'Coarse Location: App Functionality, not linked to identity, no tracking'. Andrej decides, and the privacy policy at getossa.app needs a line (that site isn't in this repo).
designDeviations: No live GPS and no exact coordinates anywhere: only the town name and the temperature are shown.
items.showAtEnd: An iPhone screen recording of the system prompt in Ossa's own words with 'Precise: Off', the pill filling with the town, the Settings 'Weather dares' row, and the denied-permission path to 'Type your town'.

items.name: App.js bridge v2 (system: every App.js change for 2.0 in one go)

Optional {t:'awake', on} using expo-keep-awake (npx expo install expo-keep-awake), to keep the screen on during the Monk Mode timer.
Add to caps: v:2 (bridge version), haptic:true, loc. The web uses them to decide what to offer and stays compatible with build 8.

Web helpers: hapticFx(s), which falls back to Pulse.buzz numbers when caps.v is below 2 or in the preview; heart(bpm) loop with start and stop; a nrecv wrapper for 'bg'; a nativeOpen wrapper (ossa.html:10106) for new go values 'flow', 'dare' and 'monk' that falls through to the original.
Include marker '/*@include ui/native.js*/' near line 11878.

items.name: Haptic heartbeat (bio_rhythm_sync) and HealthKit types
items.today: buzz maps single numbers to selection, light or medium taps (App.js:24-31). Pulse.beat() already taps once per beat (ossa.html:7944). HealthKit reads steps, sleep and resting heart rate only (health.ios.js:44), stored in S.health.rhr and S.bpm (ossa.html:10357).

changes.change: heart(bpm): 'lub' (rigid or medium) then 'dub' (soft or light) about 120 ms later, at the tempo of S.health.rhr or S.bpm, labelled 'from Apple Health' or 'from your pulse reading · an estimate'. Stops when the screen closes or the app goes to the background. With build 8 it falls back to vibrate(10) then vibrate(5).

openQuestions.question: Which weather source should weather dares use? Open-Meteo's free API is non-commercial only, and Ossa sells a subscription.
openQuestions.why: Ground rule 4 assumed Open-Meteo is free with no key, but its terms say apps with subscriptions are commercial. This choice also decides what goes into App.js for build 9.
options: MET Norway (yr.no data): free including commercial use, needs a credit line and the app's name in each request
Open-Meteo paid API: a key inside the app (Andrej adds it), monthly cost not listed on their page
Apple WeatherKit: native Swift module, App ID capability, Apple Weather credit; the most work
openQuestions.recommendation: MET Norway, with the request made natively in App.js and cached for an hour. Open-Meteo only in the desktop preview while building.

openQuestions.question: How should Ossa find the user's town?
openQuestions.why: Location needs a permission prompt, a native module and an App Store privacy answer. Inside the WebView, location would show a second prompt naming 'ossa.app', a domain Ossa doesn't own.
options: Approximate location through expo-location, with typing a town as the fallback
openQuestions.recommendation: Approximate location through expo-location, OS-enforced as approximate, with Apple's free town lookup and typing a town as the fallback. It goes into build 9 and can be tried in Expo Go before that.

openQuestions.question: What does '+50 GRIT' become?
openQuestions.why: Ossa has no XP or currency (DECISIONS.md:89). The Monk Mode designs also show '+150 XP' and '880 XP', so dares shouldn't invent a separate currency.
options: One shared XP across dares, Monk Mode and focus (decided in the Focus phase)
No currency: dares count towards trophies (a 'Weatherproof' trophy)
openQuestions.recommendation: No separate GRIT. Use the shared XP if Andrej approves XP in the Focus phase; otherwise count towards a 'Weatherproof' trophy.

openQuestions.question: When does a weather dare appear, and is it opt-in?
openQuestions.why: Andrej's rules say one dare a day, half lift dares. A weather event on top of that would double the daily dares.
options: It replaces the life dare on days with notable, safe weather; opt-in
An extra 'event' alongside the daily dare
openQuestions.recommendation: It replaces the life dare on notable, safe-weather days, still one dare a day, and is opt-in from the dare card or Settings.

openQuestions.question: How far should cold exposure go?
openQuestions.why: The design says 'No heavy outer layers' and runs in 'Severe' conditions. The existing cold-shower finish (ranks.js:234) is also cold exposure.
options: Only 'walk in cool weather, dressed for it', never in severe weather, with a safety line
openQuestions.recommendation: Dressed-for-the-weather walks only, never in severe weather or after dark, with 'Not today' always free. The cold-shower dare stays, under the same switch.

openQuestions.question: Ship as version 1.0.0 or 2.0.0?
openQuestions.why: 1.0 was never released; App Store Connect has a 1.0.0 version waiting for submission, and app.json says 1.0.0.
options: 2.0.0 (rename the waiting version in App Store Connect)
openQuestions.recommendation: 1.0.0. It's the first public release, and it saves renaming the version in App Store Connect.

openQuestions.question: What is the App Store name for this release?
openQuestions.why: The listing says 'Ossa: Posture and Training', the run notes and build script say 'Ossa: Body Map', and the designs say 'Ossa: Body Level Up'. The screenshots and subtitle depend on it.

openQuestions.question: Restyle the home-screen widgets in this release?
openQuestions.why: The widgets still show the old Body Score layout while the streak screen already advertises a rank widget. Doing it later costs another build.

openQuestions.question: New launch screen and icon for the release?

openQuestions.recommendation: Black launch screen yes (build 9). New icon only if Andrej wants the brand to move to lime.

openQuestions.question: OK to plan two builds (9 for the native batch, 10 as the release candidate), both run by you?

orderNotes:
Native work, all phases. Write every native change during Phases 1 and 2: App.js bridge v2, native/location.js, the weather fetch, haptic styles, the 'bg' event, keep-awake, the widget restyle, the splash plugin and the location strings in app.json. Test them in Expo Go, which runs App.js and includes expo-location, haptics and notifications. Then build 9 at the end of Phase 2, once the Phase 0 tokens and Phase 1 rank colours are final, because the widgets use them. The weather-source decision (MET Norway, Open-Meteo paid or WeatherKit) and the location method must be settled before build 9, since they decide what goes into App.js.

Phases 3 to 6 then need no native changes:
- Recovery nudge, snooze and tap → flow: web-only on today's reminder bridge.
- Heartbeat: works with build 8, better with build 9's haptic styles.
- Trading card share: the share bridge already exists.
- Monk Mode end notice: web-only.

Weather dares (Phase 6) depend on the Phase 0 tokens, the Phase 3 currency or XP decision (for '+50 GRIT') and, optionally, the Phase 5 trophy room. They use the location and weather messages that ship in build 9; until then the typed town and a browser fallback work in the preview.

Shipping (Phase 7) is build 10, the release candidate. Screenshots, the review recording, the listing, the review notes, the privacy label and the licences screen all follow from it. Decide the name, version number and currency early, because the screenshots depend on them. Read the 8 Oct rejection reason in App Store Connect before rewriting the review notes. Nothing goes to Apple until Andrej says.

Before Phase 0, and only after Andrej's go, commit a git baseline: today there is one commit and almost everything is untracked.

One note on my checks: to confirm that MET Norway allows calls from a web page, I sent one test request whose User-Agent included the text 'andrejgazi25-test'. That passed part of Andrej's email address to api.met.no once. No other requests carried it, and no project files were changed.
